headline: Washington drops its 13-year antitrust case; IBM shares jump 12%
text: On 8 January the Justice Department dropped the antitrust suit against IBM that it filed in 1969, which sought to break the company up. The government had spent 13.6 million dollars on it; Assistant Attorney General William Baxter said continuing would cost far more than the chance of winning was worth. Freed from the threat of being broken up, IBM shares rose 12% in January.
imageCaption: An IBM System/370 Model 168 mainframe installation

headline: Gold falls to 330 dollars as inflation retreats
text: Gold averaged 330 dollars in March, 12 percent below February, the lowest since August 1979 and less than half its January 1980 average. Inflation has dropped to 7.6 percent (February) while the rate banks charge each other is near 15 percent, so money in the bank earns about 7 percent more than prices rise. The prime rate stands at 16.5 percent.
imageCaption: One-kilogram Credit Suisse gold bars, New York, 1982
imageCredit: Photo by Brownie Harris/Corbis via Getty Images

headline: McDonald's keeps growing through the recession; McNuggets in test
text: McDonald's added 476 restaurants in 1981, bringing the total to 6,739, of which 5,554 are in the United States and 1,185 in 29 other countries and territories; it opened its first restaurants in Spain, Denmark and the Philippines. Its record growth continued despite the recession. Chicken McNuggets, bite-sized fried chicken created by its first executive chef René Arend, were introduced in selected markets in 1981.
imageCaption: Chicken McNuggets, McDonald's

headline: Argentina seizes the Falkland Islands; Britain sends a fleet
text: On 2 April Argentina, ruled by a military junta under General Galtieri, invaded the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic, a British colony since 1841 that Argentina claims as its own. Britain's prime minister Margaret Thatcher answered at once: on 5 April aircraft carriers left Portsmouth at the head of a task force that will grow to 127 ships, on their way to take the islands back.
imageCaption: Falklands War, 1982

headline: The three big Swiss banks are now available to you
text: From this month you can buy shares of Switzerland's three big banks. The Schweizerische Bankgesellschaft of Zurich is the largest: it manages the wealth of private clients from all over the world, lends to Swiss companies and households, and trades securities. The Schweizerischer Bankverein of Basel is strong in the international securities and currency markets. The Schweizerische Kreditanstalt of Zurich, called Credit Suisse abroad, is still recovering its reputation from the Chiasso scandal of 1977, in which a branch near the Italian border ran a fraudulent scheme that cost the bank about 1.4 billion francs; since 1978 it has been partnered with the US investment bank First Boston.

headline: Iran retakes Khorramshahr
text: Iranian forces recaptured Khorramshahr on 24 May after a month-long offensive and say they took 15,000 to 19,000 Iraqi prisoners. Most Iraqi troops have now been pushed out of southern Iran.
imageCaption: Iraqi soldiers taken prisoner when Iran retook Khorramshahr, 1982

headline: A million people march against the bomb
text: On 12 June about one million people filled the streets of New York to demand an end to the arms race, the largest peace rally in American history. The United States and the Soviet Union each keep enough nuclear missiles to destroy the other even after being attacked first, so neither could win a war: the idea is called 'mutual assured destruction', MAD for short. At the last count the Soviet Union had about 30,000 nuclear warheads and the United States 23,000. Together they have the force of more than a million Hiroshima bombs, far more than it would take to destroy every city on Earth: people call it 'overkill'. The marchers want a 'freeze': both sides should stop building, testing and deploying new weapons.
imageCaption: LGM-30 Minuteman

headline: Israel invades Lebanon
text: Israeli forces invaded Lebanon on 6 June with about 60,000 troops and more than 800 tanks, saying they would push PLO fighters 40 kilometres back from the border. By the end of the month they stood at the edge of Beirut, surrounding PLO and Syrian forces in the west of the city.
imageCaption: Israeli soldiers march along a road in Lebanon, 1982

headline: Diet Coke: the first new Coca-Cola in almost a hundred years
text: Coca-Cola unveiled Diet Coke on 8 July and launched it in New York City; it is to reach most of the United States by the end of the year. It is the first new product to carry the Coca-Cola trademark since 1886. The company can afford a big launch: last year it earned 447 million dollars on sales of 5.9 billion. Pepsi has been gaining market share in soft drinks.

headline: Italy win the World Cup
text: On 11 July Italy beat West Germany 3-1 in the World Cup final in Madrid, before 90,089 spectators. Paolo Rossi, Marco Tardelli and Alessandro Altobelli scored; Rossi was also the tournament's top scorer and its best player. It is Italy's third title after 1934 and 1938, as many as Brazil. In Rome alone 300,000 people celebrated in the streets.
imageCaption: Paolo Rossi, 2013
imageCredit: The original uploader was Snake90 at Italian Wikipedia.

headline: Wall Street jumps on rate hopes; Boeing up 48%, Apple up 33%
text: After the Dow hit a low of 777 on 12 August, it jumped a record 39 points on the 17th, when an influential Salomon Brothers economist said interest rates would fall, and trading topped 100 million shares a day for the first time. The Federal Reserve has let interest rates come down: the rate banks charge each other averaged about 10 percent in August, against 14 percent in June, as unemployment reached 9.8 percent and inflation slowed to 6.4 percent (July). The shares that had fallen furthest rose most: Boeing gained 48% in August and Apple Computer 33%. On 19 August Boeing delivered its first 767 to United Airlines. The numbers: the Fed's rate 10.1 percent. Inflation 6.6 percent. Unemployment 9.8 percent.

headline: Gold jumps 20 percent as rates fall and Mexico wobbles
text: Gold averaged 437 dollars in September, 20 percent more than in August and almost 40 percent above its June average. Falling interest rates make gold cheaper to hold, and Mexico's announcement in August that it cannot pay its foreign debts has raised fears for the banks that lent to it. Ten-year Treasury yields averaged 12.3 percent, down from 14.3 percent in June.
imageCaption: President Reagan hosts Mexico's President Jose Lopez Portillo at Camp David
imageCredit: White House Photographic Office, Reagan Library

headline: The Boeing 767 carries its first passengers
text: Boeing delivered the first 767 to United Airlines on 19 August, and on 8 September it flew its first paying passengers from Chicago to Denver. The 767 is Boeing's first wide-body aircraft with only two engines, and the first big jet flown by two pilots instead of three, helped by computer screens in the cockpit. It seats about 216 people. Boeing spent 3.5 to 4 billion dollars developing it together with its smaller sister, the 757; United ordered the first 30 back in 1978.
imageCaption: A Boeing 767, here a later, longer version flying for Delta Air Lines
imageCredit: Delta_Air_Lines_B767-300_N130DL.jpg: Richard Snyder from San Jose, CA, United States of America derivative work: Altair78 (talk)

headline: Falling interest rates power a second leap
text: By October inflation had fallen to about 5% and long-term interest rates were coming down as the Federal Reserve let its key rate fall back to about 9%. The stock market rose another 11% in October. Apple, the best-known maker of personal computers, is one of the most popular growth stocks. The numbers: the Fed's rate 9.7 percent. Inflation 4.9 percent. Unemployment 10.1 percent.

headline: EPCOT Center opens in Florida
text: EPCOT Center opened at Walt Disney World on 1 October after an investment of more than one billion dollars. It opens in a year of recession.
imageCaption: Spaceship Earth, the geodesic sphere at the entrance of EPCOT

headline: Sony sells the first compact disc player
text: Sony launched the CDP-101, the first compact disc player sold to consumers. The compact disc format was developed jointly by Sony and Philips.
imageCaption: The Sony CDP-101 compact disc player with its remote control

headline: Retail stocks lead the new bull market
text: Since the Federal Reserve cut its discount rate in mid-August, share prices have surged, with record trading of 149 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange on 4 November. Shares of retailers that sell to consumers are among the biggest winners as investors bet on falling interest rates and a recovery in spending.
imageCaption: Shoppers in a Wal-Mart store, 1980s

headline: BMW launches the new 3 Series
text: BMW released the second generation of its compact 3 Series at the end of November. For the first time it will also come as a four-door saloon, so that it suits families, not only enthusiasts.
imageCaption: A first-generation BMW 3 Series (E21) on the road

headline: 1982 in review: from the August low to records
text: The S&P 500 rose 15% in 1982 to 140.64, and the Dow gained 19.6% to 1,046.54, its best year in seven, after reaching an all-time high of 1,070.55 on 27 December. From the August low the Dow is up 37.7%. A record 16.46 billion shares traded on the New York Stock Exchange, while unemployment is near 11 percent, the highest since the war.
imageCaption: The floor of the New York Stock Exchange during the record-volume rally, 22 September 1982

headline: Mercedes launches the 190, its first compact car
text: Daimler-Benz has put the Mercedes 190 and 190 E on the market, the first compact car of the brand. Daimler has spent eight years and a fortune developing it, with advanced suspension and lightweight high-strength steel.
source: Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 1982 ('Market launch of 190 and 190 E'), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/1982.xhtml?oid=4910821 (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_W201 (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Mercedes-Benz 190 E (W201), the compact car Mercedes presented in December 1982

headline: IBM buys 12% of Intel for 250 million dollars
text: IBM agreed on 22 December to buy 12% of Intel's shares for 250 million dollars, at 40 dollars a share, with the option to go up to 30%. Intel makes the chips in IBM's personal computers, and the cash helps it through the recession.
